sections.h2: Does Delaware have an estate tax or inheritance tax today?
sections.html:
No. Delaware has neither tax for people who die after December 31, 2017. The estate tax was repealed for individuals dying after that date by 81 Del. Laws c. 52 (HB 16).

The inheritance tax went first. Chapter 13 of Title 30 of the Delaware Code, the inheritance tax chapter, now carries the label "Repealed." A 1998 law ended the inheritance tax effective January 1, 1999 and reshaped the estate tax so it applied only to estates large enough to need a federal estate tax return.

For heirs planning to sell a Delaware house, that is good news about one cost and no news about the others. The state does not tax the inheritance itself, but a sale can still trigger realty transfer tax and county property tax, and possibly federal rules.

sections.h2: How the estate tax worked before repeal
sections.html:
For deaths before January 1, 2018, Delaware taxed the value of an estate at death, using the federal estate tax as its starting point. This matters if the person who owned your house died in 2017 or earlier.

A resident's Delaware taxable estate was the modified federal taxable estate, reduced but not below zero by the federal applicable exclusion amount. For 2017 that exclusion was $5,490,000 for an individual. Rates were graduated, with a top rate capped at 16%.

DateChange
July 1, 1998 (effective January 1, 1999)Inheritance tax repealed; estate tax revised to follow the federal return requirement
July 1, 2009Estate tax effectively reinstated with a four-year sunset
March 28, 2013Sunset eliminated
July 2, 2017 (effective January 1, 2018)Estate tax repealed for individuals dying after December 31, 2017

sections.h2: An owner who died before 2018 and an estate still open
sections.html:
The old rules may still matter. Ask the Register of Wills or an estate attorney. The repealed sections of Chapter 15 of Title 30 carry notes pointing to 81 Del. Laws c. 52, section 2 on how the repeal applies. The old filing rules were these.

  • The return and the tax were due within nine months after the date of death.
  • The Division of Revenue could extend filing and payment time on written request. If the federal return was extended, the Delaware return was extended for a like period.
  • Interest ran at one-half of one percent per month on late tax, and penalties could include a failure-to-pay penalty of 1% per month up to 25%.
  • For nonresidents, a special lien attached to Delaware real and tangible property until the tax was paid.

The Sussex County Register of Wills publishes form NDETRR99, an affidavit that no Delaware estate tax return is required, for decedents who died from January 1, 1999 through December 31, 2017. The personal representative or a surviving joint tenant signs it before a notary, lists any Delaware real property, and cites 30 Del. C. 1505. An older estate that never cleared title may need that paper before a buyer will close.

sections.h2: Federal estate tax and a Delaware house
sections.html:
Federal estate tax reaches only very large estates. The basic exclusion amount is $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026, up from $13,990,000 for 2025. A surviving spouse can elect to take over the decedent's unused exclusion on a timely filed estate tax return, an election available since January 1, 2011.

One house rarely comes close. If the estate holds many assets, or you are unsure, ask a CPA or estate attorney.

sections.h2: Realty transfer tax when an inherited house changes hands
sections.html:
Sometimes it applies. Delaware's realty transfer tax is separate from the estate tax, and some family transfers are excluded. The rules are in Chapter 54 of Title 30.

Section 5401(1) says a taxable "document" does not include a will or a transfer on death deed. It also leaves out conveyances between spouses, between parent and child or the child's spouse, between siblings, half siblings or step siblings, and between grandparent and grandchild or the grandchild's spouse.

A sale to an outside buyer is different. Under section 5402, the rate is 3% of value, or 2.5% where the county or municipality has enacted the full 1.5% local tax. The combined state and local total is 4%, with 2.5% to the state and 1.5% to the county or municipality. The tax is split equally between grantor and grantee, and under section 5412, unless the parties agree otherwise, the grantor bears the burden of paying. Estates and trusts are listed among grantor categories without a special exemption, so if a personal representative signs the deed, confirm the treatment with the county Recorder of Deeds.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited Delaware house, step by step
sections.html:
The process runs through probate, title and the county. Delaware's three counties, New Castle, Kent and Sussex, each have their own Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds, so the office you deal with depends on where the house sits.

  1. Open the estate with the Register of Wills in the county and have the personal representative appointed.
  2. Resolve any open estate tax paperwork if the death was before 2018.
  3. Pay or settle county and school property taxes. Under Title 9, taxes in New Castle and Sussex are due July 1 and in Kent June 1.
  4. Sign a deed and pay realty transfer tax at recording, with proof of payment on the document. Under section 5408, a deed without it cannot be recorded.
  5. Deliver the house in the condition the contract requires. A cash sale can be as-is.

Late county taxes cost money. In New Castle County the collecting authority adds a 6% penalty after September 1 plus 1% a month on the unpaid balance. In Kent and Sussex, a penalty of 1.5% per month starts after September 30 of the year the tax duplicate is delivered.

Delaware is mostly owner-occupied. About 73.0% of housing units are owner-occupied, and the statewide median value of an owner-occupied home is $352,000. That figure covers the whole state and is no appraisal of any one house.

If you inherited a Delaware house you do not want to keep, a cash buyer can close as-is. That spares repairs and clean-out on a property in a distant county. Terms vary by house, and an attorney should review the estate side.

faqs.q: Is there a Delaware inheritance tax?
faqs.a: No. Chapter 13 of Title 30, the inheritance tax chapter, is marked repealed, and the repeal took effect January 1, 1999.

faqs.q: When was the Delaware estate tax repealed?
faqs.a: It was repealed for individuals dying after December 31, 2017. The repeal was approved July 2, 2017 as 81 Del. Laws c. 52 (HB 16).

faqs.q: What is the federal estate tax exclusion for 2026?
faqs.a: The basic exclusion amount is $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026, compared with $13,990,000 for 2025.

faqs.q: Do I pay realty transfer tax if I inherit a Delaware house?
faqs.a: A will and a transfer on death deed are not taxable documents, and conveyances between parent and child, siblings, and grandparent and grandchild are also excluded under 30 Del. C. 5401. A sale to an outside buyer is taxed at a combined 4%, split equally between buyer and seller unless the contract says otherwise.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for an inherited Delaware house?
faqs.a: Record it with the Recorder of Deeds in the county where the property is located. Proof of realty transfer tax payment, or an affidavit explaining why none is owed, must accompany the document.
